subject: Water Connectivity Fee and Utility Infrastructure
overview: The City Council requested reports on municipal contracts and pothole damage claims, while debating accountability for utility companies regarding gas leaks and road excavations. Significant discussion occurred regarding a proposed water connectivity fee and the installation of Massport noise monitors in residential neighborhoods.

items.title: Collective Bargaining Report
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a comprehensive report on the status of all current and pending collective bargaining agreements for the city and school department.

items.title: Natural Gas Leak Ordinance
items.summary: Approved a resolution to hold a Committee of the Whole meeting to discuss an ordinance mandating the repair of Level 3 natural gas leaks by utility companies.

items.title: Road Defect and Pothole Claims
items.summary: Approved a request for the city solicitor to report the number of property and personal injury claims filed due to potholes and other street defects in 2016 and 2017.

items.title: Fern Road Speeding and Safety
items.summary: Approved a resolution to install temporary speed bumps and increase police patrols on Fern Road following reports of excessive speeding.

items.title: Wireless Communication Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance to regulate the placement of wireless communication towers to the Committee of the Whole for further vetting.

items.title: Massport Noise Monitors
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that Massport provide and install noise monitoring devices in South Medford, Medford Heights, and at the Andrews School.

items.title: Hegner Center Site Plan
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a future use plan and building condition assessment for the reacquired Hegner Center site at Maple Park.

items.title: Medford Square Lighting Upgrades
items.summary: Approved a request for the administration to provide a status report and implementation schedule for lighting upgrades in Medford Square.

items.title: Public Video Monitoring Feasibility
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a feasibility study and cost analysis for implementing video monitoring in public parks, buildings, and intersections.

items.title: Routine Infrastructure Signage
items.summary: Approved resolutions to replace a stop sign on Midwood Street, replace crossing barrels at the Columbus School with permanent signs, and restore a Veterans Memorial sign on Main Street.

items.title: Legislative Management Software
items.summary: Accepted a committee report recommending the procurement of software for video streaming and digital management of agendas and minutes for all city boards and commissions.

items.title: Utility Excavation Permit Standards
items.summary: Accepted a committee report requesting a legal opinion on the city's ability to limit or place moratoriums on excavation permits for utility companies.

items.title: Water Connectivity Fee and Hotel Petition
items.summary: Received and placed on file a petition regarding the new water connectivity fee and a proposed hotel project following public testimony criticizing the fee as an unfair tax.
